valuation_philosophy: Owner-FCF DCF on a 10-year explicit horizon. SBC (incl. equity-award taxes) is fully EXPENSED and the diluted share count held FLAT -- never both. Interest income is excluded from the flows (the cash pile is added separately in the bridge). Cash tax ramps to ~21%. Margins are built from EBITDA/SBC/D&A/tax/capex/WC each year rather than carrying the latest margin forward. Terminal value = Gordon, capped at 20x terminal owner FCF. Superseded the earlier 5-year, company-FCF-seeded model: see methodology_notes.supersedes.

inputs.shares_basis: weighted-avg fully diluted, Q2-26 (basic 25.5M); held FLAT per SBC-expensing policy
inputs.net_debt_note: Cash 45.715 less borrowings 87.950 less contingent consideration ~3.7 less IFRS-16 lease liabilities 5.818 (leases-as-debt treatment). Verified against the Q2-2026 6-K. The open $70M SIB at $20.40 (expires 26-Aug-26) is NOT baked in -- the stock trades above the offer.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: owner FCF = OCF 28.173 - capex 0.981; NOT the company-defined 38.4
inputs.sbc_note: IFRS share-based compensation FY2025 $5.998M (FY2024 $7.330M, FY2023 $6.049M), per the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation in the Q4-2025 press release and the FY2025 40-F (ifrs-full:ExpenseFromSharebasedPaymentTransactionsWithEmployees). At 2.5% of revenue SBC is modest for a SaaS name. Shares are held flat in this model, so SBC is expensed rather than diluted (see sbc-flat-share-count policy). Separately, acquisition-related compensation of $4.390M FY2025 is comp expense that management adds back to both Adjusted EBITDA and its Free Cash Flow measure -- see fcf_definition_note.
inputs.fcf_definition_note: Docebo's reported Free Cash Flow ADDS BACK acquisition-related compensation, transaction costs and restructuring paid. FY2025: OCF 28.173 - capex 0.981 = 27.192 owner FCF vs 38.377 reported (11.185 of add-backs). Q2-2026 makes the point sharper: OCF was NEGATIVE 3.073, and 7.311 of add-backs turn it into a reported +3.066. Acquisition-related comp has recurred every year (0.858 -> 3.976 -> 6.235) and is treated here as a real, recurring cost.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders equity turned negative ($(0.6M) at Q1-2026) after the $60M SIB and $61M 365Talents acquisition were largely debt-financed; equity CAGR is therefore not usable as a growth anchor. EPS CAGR of 300% reflects profitability ramp from near-zero, not a sustainable forward rate. FCF growth rates are used as the primary anchor, with revenue growth as the guardrail (11.9% FY2025 actual, guidance ~12% for FY2026).
historical_growth.note_on_3yr_5yr: Only 3 clean annual data points available (FY2022, FY2023, FY2024, FY2025). FCF was negligible in FY2022 ($0.8M), so 3-yr FCF CAGR is unusable. Revenue 3yr CAGR of 19.1% reflects faster early growth; the business has decelerated to ~12% as it scales.

entry_price.methodology: Price giving a 15% IRR to that scenario's value; weighted by scenario probability.
entry_price.note: Weighted 15%-hurdle entry $21.84 vs price $23.02 -- the model clears its hurdle by only -5%.

probability_weighted.band_note: House (SBC expensed) $39.07 vs street (SBC non-cash) $45.96. Price $23.02 sits BELOW both, so a 0-100% band position is not meaningful here.

checks_run.note: 56% of value is terminal; the 20x cap never binds, so this rests on the 3.0% Gordon rate.
Entry $21.84 vs price $23.02 -- clears the hurdle by only 5%.

investment_thesis.key_insight: At $23.02 Docebo trades near 2.2x forward revenue with 12-14% core ARR growth and a margin path management is guiding upward (FY2026 raised three times). The owner-FCF base is $27.2M, not the $38.4M headline -- the difference is restructuring and acquisition earn-out comp the company adds back. Q2-2026 shows why that matters: operating cash flow was negative $3.1M. The bull case rests on skills/knowledge attach and post-OEM reacceleration making the good outcome likelier rather than bigger; the bear on 'restructuring' proving permanent.
key_risks: Intercap ~56.6% control with a shrinking float
Negative book equity (-$0.3M) after debt-funded buybacks; net debt now $52M
Restructuring paid rose to $4.7M in Q2-26, against a base case assuming it tapers by 2028
AWS Skill Builder, Dayforce OEM and Salesforce all departed; terminal fade is the key judgment

methodology_notes.fcf_approach: Owner FCF: NOPAT + D&A - capex - WC, with SBC expensed and shares flat.
methodology_notes.wacc_calculation: Single 10.5% WACC across ALL scenarios. Scenario-varying the discount rate double-counts optimism, since the growth path already carries the scenario view.
methodology_notes.terminal_growth: 1.5% bear / 3.0% base / 3.5% bull; Gordon capped at 20x terminal owner FCF.
methodology_notes.terminal_cap_note: The 20x cap does NOT bind at these inputs -- it engages only above g > 5.24%. Realised exit multiples are 11.3x/13.7x/14.8x, so terminal value rests on Gordon alone.
methodology_notes.net_debt_treatment: IFRS-16 treatment (A): leases as debt in the bridge, no lease principal in the flows, renewal carried in the 0.5% capex line.
methodology_notes.shares_outstanding: Held flat at 26.8M diluted. SBC expensing substitutes for grant dilution.
methodology_notes.supersedes: Replaces the 5-year, company-FCF-seeded model (weighted IV $33.00 on $17.52-era inputs, 25/55/20 weights, 9.5% bull WACC). That model understated net debt by $36M, used the company-defined FCF of $38.4M as its base, and discounted its bull case more generously than house discipline allows. Reports/DCBO_DCF_Model.xlsx is the retired workbook for it.
methodology_notes.open_judgments: Two judgments carry most of the value vs the retired model: franchise life beyond 2030 (10-yr fade vs 5-yr stop, ~+$6.30) and the 35% bull weight (~+$5.00). Intercap holds ~56.6%, so bull-case value may not accrue to minorities on the same terms. Falsification points: reported-vs-core ARR convergence at Q3-26 (5-6 Nov), NDR trend, government/healthcare traction.
